request.query:
mutation CreateService($name: String!, $ownerId: String, $environmentId: String, $type: String, $repo: String, $image: String, $registryCredentialId: String, $branch: String, $rootDir: String, $runtime: String, $buildCommand: String, $startCommand: String, $dockerfilePath: String, $buildFilter: BuildFilterInput, $plan: String, $autoDeploy: Boolean, $schedule: String, $command: String, $publishPath: String, $port: Int, $envVars: [EnvVarInput], $secretFiles: [SecretFileInput]) {
  createService(
    name: $name
    ownerId: $ownerId
    environmentId: $environmentId
    type: $type
    repo: $repo
    image: $image
    registryCredentialId: $registryCredentialId
    branch: $branch
    rootDir: $rootDir
    runtime: $runtime
    buildCommand: $buildCommand
    startCommand: $startCommand
    dockerfilePath: $dockerfilePath
    buildFilter: $buildFilter
    plan: $plan
    autoDeploy: $autoDeploy
    schedule: $schedule
    command: $command
    publishPath: $publishPath
    port: $port
    envVars: $envVars
    secretFiles: $secretFiles
  ) {
    id
    name
    type
    phase
    projectId
    environmentId
    registryCredentialId
    latestDeployId
    __typename
  }
}

FreshDesktopSettings.health:
- text: Health Checks Configure the HTTP path bex polls periodically to monitor your service. Health Check Path An HTTP path bex polls to decide whether your service is healthy; it must answer 2xx or 3xx within 5 seconds, and 60 seconds of consecutive failures restarts the instance — point it at a cheap route. Leave it empty to check only that the process is listening on its port — the right choice when the service has no cheap route that returns 2xx.
- textbox "Health Check Path" [disabled]:
  - /placeholder: Empty — check the port only
- button "Edit Health Check Path"
FreshDesktopSettings.port:
- text: Port The port your container listens on. bex routes traffic to it and injects it as $PORT. Port The port your container listens on (default 3000). bex routes traffic to it, injects it as $PORT, and refuses PORT as an environment variable because of it. Saving starts a new deploy and restarts the instances.
- spinbutton "Port" [disabled]: "8846"
- button "Edit Port"

scopeNotes: Cancellation focus and Enter reopening were live-tested on text and number rows at1440x1000 and a fresh390x844 page; Health Check Path native keyboard Cancel uses actual Tab then Enter. Pointer Edit was also used for that Cancel trial and successful saves.
The final fresh desktop replay used64 actual Tab presses with no programmatic focus. The first desktop hash-targeted page needed1 Tab; those entry conditions are recorded separately, not conflated.

The original implementation has six maintained regressions covering text/number/keyboard-Cancel, Select popup-only Escape, Combobox explicit Cancel and no focus steal. Their historical pass remains historical; no suite rerun or product test/source change in this acceptance filing.
Select/Combobox live cancellation, sibling service/datastore types, aliases, restricted/busy/unmount scenarios, Chinese UI, other browsers and authenticated Render focus were not reaccepted.
Successful save still leaves BODY focused and returns the saved disabled input; changing that focus policy was explicitly outside293. No new issue is claimed for it.

Zero mutations were captured inside the Escape and port-validation trials; the independent canonical state after all six primary desktop/mobile cases and validation retained one original Live deploy and the original settings. The Cancel factory did not install a separate request listener, so it is not itself a zero-write network receipt.

One native DeployActions read aborted during navigation; no other captured transport failure and no console errors. Explicit independent page.request probes retain their own receipts, outside the native network snapshot.

Wrong Save label was corrected to Save changes before any submit. The first native network dump exceeded the local stdout cap; the same live browser/log was reread with a larger output budget after logout. No browser restart, write replay or product failure was inferred.
No paid action or pre-existing-resource mutation. Only owned exact App/name IDs and labels were inspected for physical cleanup.
